cartoons.caption: "Two minutes' silence, and the station manager wants to know who is sponsoring it."
"The referee says wide, the captain says over, and the ground has retained counsel."
"The company's engineers find the train is quieter when stopped. They are now studying whether it is also cheaper."
"Enter it in the log, Mister: we are leading from behind."
"Cold? Madam, this is the coldest morning since the war. You ought to be proud to be here for it."
"One more 'Good King Wenceslas' and 1978 will have a low opinion of us." "It will have to wait its turn."
"One valve left, sir. Will you be wanting Christmas, or the scores?"
"Six hundred men to keep order at midnight, boys. And by a quarter past I'll want to know who has my helmet."
"The committee declares the race a success and the lake in breach of contract."
"The horse will go out at seven and report. The foreman will follow on receipt of the report."
"Brethren, the sermon is postponed for want of one valve. The collection will proceed by the usual means."
"He eats the same as the taxpayer. He just does it first."
"Mr. Aaronson has had the sermon four times this winter. Mr. Zwick is beginning to doubt."
"The sergeant has no objection to the dancing, provided nobody enjoys it."
"He has given up listening for Lent, Father." "How can you tell?" "We can't."
"My boy won. It's only the record, the referee and the other fella say different."
"The Clerk's machine has recorded the gentleman's remarks, and asks to be excused."
"The robin has been recorded, catalogued and thanked by the committee. It has gone to New Jersey."
"Nine seconds short of last year, Alderman. May I suggest you go round again, and look less like yourself?"
"Two trunks of records for the training camp, and not one of them can hit a curve."
"And now, listeners, the hat on my left. It is, I am informed, a hat."
"The promoter would dance himself, only somebody has to be exhausted by the receipts."
"That dog is the only voter in the ward who has gone through the candidate thoroughly."
"The Commissioner reports the fire is under control. It has agreed to stay on the twenty-six acres it already has."
"Never late, never rude, and he has yet to ask for a raise. The Company has sent a man round to have a word with him."
"The Company has retired the horse. Nobody has been able to retire the horse from the Company."
"Eleven months I'm too busy, Ma. Today the whole borough's too busy, so I'm in line with the rest of them."
"The experts agree the mud was the deciding factor. The mud has been asked for its selections next year."
"Mr. Peck wishes it known he is not against the veterans, only against hearing them go by."
"Why go to Coney? We've got the noise right here, and nobody wants a hot dog."
"Gentlemen, my horse has been libelled in forty-one entries, and I have brought the list."
"Dawn came up on time and the machine was still warming. The Secretary has asked it to go back."
"I assure you the ocean is there, madam. I paid a nickel for it."
"Your wall has its licence, sir, and I'm bound to say it has the better record of the two of you."
"A lady on the committee, gentlemen. We shall have to begin reading the minutes."
"The boy knew his name, his street and his number. The father, when located, knew two of them."
"Six thousand bathers, and the Commissioner is the only one who brought his hat."
"Thirty-one guests, no speeches, no minutes. The Alderman came anyway, and has been given a seat by the door."
"There. Hear her? Engines. Coming in from the east." "That's my brother-in-law."
"Each gentleman would know that bark anywhere, Your Honour. The dog would like to go home."
"If any man knows cause why these two may not be joined, let him speak now. Not you."
"Twenty seasons, one carrot. The Company asks whether she can sign for it."
"That's fourteen children, one hat, and a Mr. Kowalski who says he is lost as well."
"The Board has installed a machine to take the roll. It will be absent Thursdays."
"Mr. Tilden concedes nothing to the record, the linesman or the ball."
"Nice summer? I thought about you all through it."
"Thirty years. All he ever left me was a block, a puddle and a bill, and I'm sorry to see him go."
"Mr. Mack says the starter will be announced when the starter has been told."
"The crowd asks your position on the seventh inning, Mr. President." "Tell them prosperity is rounding third."
"Let us pray." "Sell."
"The paper says stocks eased. I'd like to meet the fella that eased them, and I'd like to bring my brother."
"Forty years in the tea tin, and this week the president of the bank came round to ask how she does it."
